questions.question: Dr. RACHID must photograph a ceramic crown. Dr. REDA gives him advice to capture translucency. What should be done?
options: Use side lighting to reveal translucency
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Side lighting reveals the translucency of ceramics by creating light play.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will position a side flash.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA examines a photo of a veneer preparation. Dr. RACHID asks: 'What is the protocol for photographing a veneer preparation?'
options: Use high contrast and side lighting to reveal the margins
Take the photo from far away
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'High contrast and side lighting reveal the margins of veneer preparations.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will adjust the lighting.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of the dental arch. Dr. REDA tells him: 'The tongue is hiding the arch.' How to solve this problem?
options: Use a tongue retractor or ask the patient to position it
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A tongue retractor or clear instructions to the patient allow the dental arch to be exposed.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use a tongue retractor.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must photograph a smile with asymmetry. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'How to capture this asymmetry?'
options: Take a perfectly symmetrical frontal photo as a reference
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A perfectly symmetrical frontal photo allows documenting the asymmetry as a reference.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will take a standard frontal photo.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a frontal photo of a patient. Dr. REDA tells him: 'The head is tilted.' How to correct this problem?
options: Straighten the image in post-production or reposition the patient
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A poorly positioned patient can be corrected in post-production or by repositioning.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will check the positioning.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA examines a photo of a tooth with a composite restoration. He tells Dr. RACHID: 'The texture of the composite is not visible.' How to improve the texture?
options: Use grazing light to reveal surface texture
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Grazing light creates shadows that reveal the surface texture of composites.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will adjust the flash angle.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of the dental arch with an intraoral mirror. Dr. REDA asks him: 'How to avoid fogging on the mirror?'
options: Heat the mirror or use an anti-fog product
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Heating the mirror under hot water or using an anti-fog product prevents condensation.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will heat the mirror before.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must photograph a tooth with a filling. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'What is the particular challenge?'
options: Managing reflections from metal or composite surfaces
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Metal or composite fillings can create annoying reflections that must be controlled.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use a polarizer.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo with a color cast. Dr. REDA asks him: 'Which parameter is involved?'
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A color cast is often due to incorrect white balance or inadequate lighting.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will check the white balance.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA explains to Dr. RACHID the importance of post-production. Dr. RACHID asks: 'What edits are ethically acceptable?'
options: Adjustment of exposure, contrast, and white balance
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Ethical edits are limited to technical adjustments like exposure, contrast, and white balance.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will remain ethical in my edits.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a tooth with a cavity. Dr. REDA tells him: 'The cavity is not visible.' How to improve visualization of cavities?
options: Use high contrast and grazing light
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'High contrast and grazing light reveal cavities by creating shadows.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will adjust the lighting.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must create a clinical case presentation. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'What photos are essential?'
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A complete clinical case requires photos at each stage of treatment to document the evolution.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will document every stage.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a frontal photo of a smiling patient. Dr. REDA tells him: 'The lips are bothering.' How to manage lips in a smile photo?
options: Ask the patient to smile naturally without forcing the lips
Ask the patient to close their eyes
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A natural smile without forcing the lips gives the best aesthetic result.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will put the patient at ease.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must photograph a removable prosthesis. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'What is the protocol?'
options: Photograph the prosthesis on a neutral background with good lighting
Photograph the prosthesis only in the mouth
Photograph the prosthesis from far away
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'A removable prosthesis should be photographed on a neutral background to show all the details.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use a black background.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a tooth with a fracture. Dr. REDA asks him: 'How to highlight the fracture?'
options: Use grazing light to create shadows that reveal the fracture
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Grazing light creates shadows that highlight fractures and cracks.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will adjust the lighting.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA explains to Dr. RACHID the importance of standardization in dental photography. Dr. RACHID asks: 'Why standardize?'
options: To reliably compare photos over time
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Standardization allows reliable comparisons of clinical cases over time.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will standardize my settings.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a tooth with a gold restoration. Dr. REDA tells him: 'There is a golden reflection.' How to manage this reflection?
options: Use a polarizer or adjust white balance
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Golden reflections can be reduced with a polarizer or adjusted white balance.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use a polarizer.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must photograph a tooth with an amalgam filling. Dr. RACHID asks: 'What is the challenge?'
options: Amalgam is highly reflective and can create reflections
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Amalgam is highly reflective and can create reflections that must be managed with a polarizer.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will use a polarizer.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of the dental arch with the ring flash. Dr. REDA asks him: 'Is the light ring visible?' What is the usefulness of the light ring?
options: It creates an aesthetic reflection and helps with focusing
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'The light ring is an aesthetic reflection and can serve as a focus guide.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will ensure it is visible.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must create a clinical case portfolio. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'How to organize the photos?'
options: By clinical case, with pre, intra, and post-operative photos
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Photos should be organized by clinical case with chronological order to show evolution.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will organize my photos by case.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a patient's tongue. Dr. REDA asks him: 'What pathology can be seen on the tongue?'
options: Signs of deficiencies, infections, or systemic pathologies
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'The tongue can reveal signs of deficiencies, infections, or systemic diseases.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will always photograph the tongue.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA explains to Dr. RACHID the importance of patient consent for photos. Dr. RACHID asks: 'Why is this important?'
options: For legal and ethical reasons, the patient must give consent
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Patient consent is mandatory for legal and ethical reasons, especially if photos are used for presentations.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will always ask for consent.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID took a photo of a tooth with an interproximal cavity. Dr. REDA asks him: 'How to visualize interproximal cavities?'
options: Use high contrast and grazing light
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'High contrast and grazing light reveal interproximal cavities.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will adjust the lighting.'

questions.question: Dr. REDA must photograph a patient with gingival pigmentation. Dr. RACHID asks him: 'How to capture the pigmentation?'
options: Use grazing light and high contrast
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Grazing light and high contrast reveal gingival pigmentation.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will adjust the lighting.'

questions.question: Dr. RACHID, after having managed complex dental photography cases with Dr. REDA, receives his congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. RACHID?
options: Become an expert in clinical dental photography
questions.explanation: Dr. REDA explains: 'Mastery of complex cases is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. RACHID: 'I will deepen my skills.'
